lines.text: Ah, you're awake. I was guarding your biscuits.
From inside.
Riddle: what's yours, but your roommate uses it more?
Your NAME. But also the biscuits.
Come and see your kingdom.
Freshers chase. It's tradition. Since now.
…Don't lose that.
I'm more of a consultant.
KB sold out of candles. At noon. Who knew?
They have taken light. Welcome to university.
Plan B. Garri. Cold water only.
Hot water? You want eba by accident?
Old thing. It does that.
I'll pay with a riddle. What has keys but no door?
Two goats. Tired.
What are you looking at?
What's two metres tall and fears a hairdresser?
Sheikh Biru! Lecture us on football!
It is never simple when he says that.
Forty moths. One Professor.
Riddle me this. …No. Not tonight.
And everybody's reading. Alone.
One torch is a snack. Five is a problem.
We have a paper at eight. Why am I happy?
…That wasn't there yesterday.
Riddle: what is A4, and ruins your life?
We don't move. We are carried.
'B.B.' She signed it. So it's real.
The gym opens at seven. I'll watch. From far.
Riddle: what is free, wet, and full of fi—
Good evening to you too, Baba Ranger.
That's the garden's sound. Under WATER.
I'm the loud one. I'll stay up here and be loud.
Who are you talking to? I heard you talking!
I ironed a shirt. For radio. Is that normal?
Good… good evening. This is, um. The news.
Riddle: what goes off without warning? Our light.
EVERYBODY. Underlined. Twice. Start walking.
Riddle: what has four papers and no mercy?
Riddle: what has two owners and one mattress?
No, I'm actually asking. What do we do?
He's eating our garri. I approve of him.
It doesn't blink. Have you noticed?
We blink. It doesn't.
'Beneath the market, where people gather.'
If I see him, I make a bird call.
…Bird.
It's a rare bird. Go.
Bird! BIRD!
We have him. I feel sick. Do you feel sick?
So it CAN come down.
They're sitting on the cables. Like hens.
English, sir?
ENGINERING. One E short. Like our budget.
I'm not in this faculty. The pies don't know that.
Riddle me this: what has four suspects and—
…No. Sorry. Not funny.
This is Riddles After Dark. I'm Bature. You're awake.
And I'll need a riddle. A big one.
Riddle me this, Ring Road.
What eats light, and gives back a shopping centre?
There's a scout today. Nobody's told him. So: sh.
Riddle: what has forty poles and no lamp? Don't answer.

sections.title: Love in the Time of NEPA

lines.text: Love riddles. A hundred each. I'm rich. Don't ask me.
You have ₦300 and the truth. One of them is free.
Say am again slowly.
The mall. I drew it from memory.
Six against. Motion dies. Like our social lives.
Riddle: what holds six fools and one rope?
It's going DOWN. We broke it properly.
(Riddle: who knocks at five? No one good.)
They're asking YOU to sign. We're old. Riddle that.
Indefinite. That is not a date. That is a mood.
Was the campus always this big?
I put fifty naira in my pocket so it won't feel alone.
It has one wheel.
Mubarak, I am loyal. But I am also hungry.
I am here as a witness. Not a participant.
Witnesses stand behind. Go first.
Who hasn't finished what?
Yes, Baba Ra— yes, sir.
Riddle me this!
…It gave it back wrong. Even the hall is on strike.
Normalise sleeping in class. But not like THIS.
Finally. Someone asks me to keep talking.
School padlocks are grey. And older than us.
Breaking news: the Pastor has passed.
…The ball. He passed the ball.
Riddle me this. …No. Tomorrow. Tomorrow I'll have one.
The inside is also white. We are finished.
Quietly. 'Mu je' quietly.
You are thinking like a goalpost.
Who is paying that light bill?
Seven chairs. Six gave up. I relate to the six.
So nobody will mention the seventh chair. Fine. Fine.
Professor! Riddle me this: when is break?
Breaking news: he delivered. Like DHL with a beard.
She was this funny all along? I feel robbed.
Honestly? Everything. Sit down.
One plate, two spoons. It's called a merger.
No. Sit down. Your feet are doing something.
'King of the Spot.' 'Marry me.' 'Sells shoes, DM.'
You have fans. I have your leftover rice. Fair.
Bot. Scroll.
Tell me that's you. Tell me you have a twin.
You never do the turn right. …Oh.
Riddle me this: what comes once a year, today?
You paused. I counted the pause. Lunch at one.
That's not… Tell me that's not.
The turn. That's not your turn.
You have never once done that turn right.
Riddle me this: who is my best friend since 1900?
On what? You haven't left the bed!
You can have the riddles.
You can't have the timing. Nobody can. Even me.
Riddle me this: what has two dates and no plan?
That is the riddle. Look at it. Then look at me.
And the twins have a chart. With string.
Why do I have a column?
Forty-one planks. Last year it was thirty-nine.
Riddle me this: what did I do to deserve this?
Breaking news: I read. Don't tell my village.
Riddle me th— …No. Fine. Go well.
Look at you. Senior. Giving directions like a signboard.
I got one too. Good paper. Holds a teacup very well.
We're late. Whoever it is can wait. We can't.
Why is he in a gown? Convocation is in July.
…So we call them. Like register. I can do register.
On time? Check the sky. Check the trousers.
Riddle me this. What do you give, and keep after giving?
Your word.
Why are you counting? We're all there.
…forty-one per cent cheaper over ten years. Source: Okafor.
Riddle me this: why did I say that out loud? Ha. Joke.
Arts. Riddle me this: no. Not now. Just… here.
Why is everybody looking at me like a stranger?
Present! …Sorry. Habit.
Five years, and that's the cleanest thing you own.
A riddle. No answer. You'll get it in ten years.
Call me.
Riddle me this: what has six floors now? CALL ME.
Riddle me this: who's back? You. Hi.
Breaking news: roommate returns. Public relieved.
You're home! Did you bring food? Say yes.
Ah. You. I was just guarding your biscuits.
Riddle: what has two legs and owes me garri? Hello!
Riddle me this: who's Firdausi's favourite cousin? Me. Hi.
Ah, my cousin's roommate! Has she named another lizard?
Go well. Leave the biscuits.
Breaking news: roommate leaves. Nobody cries. Much.
Not back by ten? I'm eating your share.
Riddle for the road: … I forgot it. Go.
Stay tuned. That's radio for 'goodbye'.
Thanks. You're the second best person in this room.
Na gode. [Thank you.] {{ROOMIE}} is grateful. Rare event.
Thank you. I'll pay you back. In riddles.
Sorry. I ate the groundnut. Both bags. Riddle: who?
My bad. Really. No joke this time.
Thanks. I'll mention you on air. Anonymously. Loudly.
You look sharp. Sharper than our knife. Low bar, but still.
Look at you, reading. Breaking news.
You're good at this. Don't tell anyone I said it.
You laughed at my riddle. Nobody does that. Thank you.
You snore in three languages. One is Morse code.
Your side of the room is a crime scene. Mostly socks.
You call that cooking? That's warming with ambition.
Tell Firdausi she owes me garri. Since first year.
Lead on. I'll narrate. 'They walked bravely, and late…'
Right behind you. Counting steps. Thirty… four? Two?
Wait for me. My slippers are on strike.
I'm ageing. Visibly. Come on.
Riddle: what is slow, and also you? Hurry.
Wrong way. The Spot is that side. Food is always that side.
Breaking news: we are lost. More at eleven.
Walking with you. This is now a live outside broadcast.
Yes! Obviously! …What did I agree to?
Yes. Riddle me this: why not?
No. Riddle me this: no.
No. Not even for jollof. …Okay, maybe for jollof.
Absolutely not. {{ROOMIE}} has standards. One.
Maybe. Ask me after I eat.
Maybe. Let me consult my mattress.
Say am again slowly. [Say it again slowly.]
I read that sentence three times. It's still in Engineering.
Agreed. Shake on it. Wash first.
Team Room! Undefeated since Monday!
I'm not going. My bed has asked me to stay.
No. I'm a witness, not a participant.
Riddle: what's full of holes but holds water? Not our roof.
Riddle: what comes once and leaves forever? Light. NEPA light.
Did you eat? Is there more? Mostly the second.
Riddle me this: can I borrow your charger?
You okay? Real answer. Not the 'I'm fine' one.
Listening tonight? Ring Road FM. Say yes. Lie if needed.
Riddle me this, Ring Road: what's on air, and off light? Us.
WE WON! Breaking news! Everybody calm down! Not you!
Riddle: who's the best? Us. That was easy.
We lost. Garri tonight. Garri understands.
Next time. Mu sake. [We go again.]
Ow. I'm narrating this as assault.
You bumped me. I'll sue. In riddles.
And they fall! The crowd gasps! …I'm fine.
The floor and I are on first-name terms now.
They have taken light. Welcome to university. Again.
Riddle: what's dark and full of us? This room.
NEPA, why? We were getting along.
UP NEPA! Charge everything! Charge the kettle!
Light! Quick, iron something before it changes its mind.
Rain. Lecture's cancelled. In my heart.
Our window leaks. Breaking news: indoor rain.
It's so hot my garri is cooking itself.
The fan is turning. Slowly. Out of pity.
One plate, two spoons. It's a merger.
Is that suya? Asking for me.
Garri, sugar, groundnut, cold water. Five stars.
Sapa has entered the chat. It's sitting on my bed.
I have fifty naira and a dream. The dream is jollof.
Biscuits! You know the way to my heart. It's biscuits.
For me? I'll share it. Probably. Some of it.
Thank you. I'll keep it. Under the bed. Respectfully.
A book. Riddle: what is never opened? This.
A whole bag of groundnut? I'll name my firstborn after you.
Chin chin! The good one! You're my favourite human.
Narrator voice: and the roommate sat. And sat.
Riddle me this. …Nobody's here. I'll answer. Garri.
Forty-two stairs. Forty-three? I'll count again tomorrow.
{{ROOMIE}} is not lazy. {{ROOMIE}} is conserving energy.
Mass Comm. We communicate. Massively.
Professor! …Sorry. Wrong person. Hello, person.
Tanko gave me a riddle last year. I'm still on it.
Jega says I'm the worst striker he knows. He knows two.
You awake? …Riddle. No. Sleep. Goodnight.
Narrator voice: it was late. They were hungry. Again.
Riddles After Dark, eleven p.m. You're awake anyway.
Roommate! I saved you the corner of the bed. The cold corner.
Your matric gown is wearing you.
You wear your lanyard to the bathroom. Freshers.
Test week. I read out loud. The neighbours are reading too.
Results are up. I'm not looking. You look. Tell me gently.
Riddle me this: what has two beds and one Indomie?
The tap runs at six. I run at six-oh-one.
Breaking news: roommate attends lecture. Wrong theatre.
Small room. Big dreams. Medium garri.
I tried to read. The page read me. It won.
Mai Shayi took a riddle as payment. Legal tender.
Day one, I guarded your biscuits. A hero.
Freshers chase goats. Tradition. Since that day.
Our first jollof. Half done. NEPA finished it.
Twelve freshers, one candle, one cup of garri. Classic.
One torch is a snack. Five is a problem. I still say it.
That plank broke under me slowly. While I talked. Rude.
At the dam, you were talking to someone. I heard you.
EVERYBODY. Underlined twice. My finest document.
Fresher no more! Riddle: what's next? Second year. Easy.
Lights out. Who's scared of the dark? Not me. Stay close.
The corridor hums at night. Say it's normal. Say it.
I ironed a shirt for radio. Radio can't see shirts.
Jega's team picked me last. Correctly.
'Good evening. This is, um, the news.' My debut.
Kabiru let me read the weather. Dust. Nailed it.
Second-year! Stand up straight. Freshers are watching.
Three mall trips this week. For 'the air conditioning'.
You read. I'll make the tea. That's teamwork.
Second year. I've stopped getting lost. Mostly.
The mall never blinks. Have you noticed? I have.
Sapa level: I licked the seasoning sachet. Plain.
Riddle: what's open all night and isn't our light? The mall.
Breaking news: roommate buys power bank. Already warm.
Somebody's slippers on our floor. Eating our garri. Fine.
Bird call. Rare bird. Still practising.
So it CAN come down. The escalator. And our hopes.
ENGINERING. One E short. I still laugh.
I drew the mall. A rectangle labelled MALL. Genius.
We broke it properly. Professionally.
Three hundred naira and the truth. Still a good date.
Who knocks at five a.m.? Shamsu. With a soldering iron.
They asked US to sign. We're old now. Riddle that.
The mall is blazing. We have one candle and vibes.
Can't sleep. The mall hums. Like a fridge with ambition.
Narrator voice: they had a plan. The plan was a rectangle.
Kabiru's voice is warm bread. Mine is toast.
Decoy. That was my role. I decoyed beautifully.
Riddles After Dark. My show. My voice. My riddles.
A caller solved my riddle. I had to hang up. Jealous.
Still here? Good. I was talking to the wall. It's tired.
Teaching at Demo? Teacher! Can I have marks?
Farm work at five-thirty. A cock woke me. Personally.
Strike, day forty. I've read every label in this room.
Garri: breakfast, lunch, emotional support.
Those who stayed. That's us. A small, hungry club.
Narrator voice: the campus was empty. The roommate, hungrier.
The hall is on strike too. The taps are protesting.
Indefinite. Not a date. A mood. Still the mood.
Mai Shayi's kettle. Five of us. Best tea in history.
Mubarak's wheelbarrow has one wheel. Like my plans.
Witnesses stand behind. I stood. Very behind.
I wrote my name in the dust. Somebody wiped it. Neatly.
Thanks for sitting with me. That's all. Thanks.
Riddle me this… I have one now. Tomorrow. Promise.
Seven chairs at the Old Site. I count them in my head.
Shamsu's study group: free notes, free lamp, free lecture.
Buses! Twenty buses! The campus is loud again!
Empty campus at night. Even the crickets went home.
No light, no lectures. Just us and the fan's memory.
Garri economics: I'm the economy. I'm also the garri.
Strike radio: me, a mic, four listeners. Hi, Mum.
Ring Road FM is quiet. I talk to the transmitter.
You pulled me up. Riddle me this: tomorrow. I'll have one.
Look at you, in office shoes. Do they hurt? They hurt.
You posted that? With that caption? Bold.
Cook-off at Mama Nkechi's. I'm a judge. I'm a mouth.
IT placement: six hours at a photocopier. Employed.
We give freshers directions now. Wrong ones, but with love.
Lucky's ring light woke the whole floor.
Narrator voice: they had money. For one weekend.
Riddle: what's printed, stamped, and still not ready? IT letter.
'King of the Spot.' 'Sells shoes, DM.' Your fans.
You have fans. I have your leftover rice. Fair.
I saw you across the court. You were also here. Don't explain.
You paused before lunch. I counted the pause.
That wasn't your turn in the clip. You never do the turn right.
I hung four of Nusaiba's posters. Upside down. We won.
Payday! Riddle: who's my best friend since 1900? You.
Two dates at seven. Riddle me this: who brought groundnuts?
The pier, you, me, groundnuts. Not sad. Not sad at all.
Forty classmates want tutorials. From ME. Riddle that.
Report due tomorrow. Riddle: who hasn't started? Us.
The phone is in the tin. I'm fine. I miss it. I'm fine.
Results are out. I topped two courses. Don't tell my reputation.
My show moved to ten. Prime time. For owls.
Top in Media Law. Shh. Officially, I'm a clown.
Lucky asked for a radio collab. I gave him a riddle. He left.
Finalist! You walk like you own the ring road.
You're crying at a group photo. Again. Third one.
Final year. Forty-one stairs. Every time now.
Last semester. I'm saving every riddle for the farewell.
Breaking news: roommate submits project early. Nobody believes it.
Freshers ask US where Gabas is. We used to be them.
Narrator voice: and they lived happily. After exams.
Alhaji Needle said Thursday. Which Thursday? He won't say.
Senior! Giving directions like a signboard.
Fresher tax, reversed. We pay them now. In zobo.
Your project smoked. The whole lawn watched. In nightclothes.
I got a letter too. Good paper. Holds tea well.
On time to dinner? Check the sky. Check the outfit.
What do you give and keep after giving? Your word.
I said something smart at my defence. Still shaking.
Everybody looked at me like a stranger. Never again, please.
Last nights in this room. Don't make it weird. …Too late.
Riddle me this: what will I miss? …Don't make me say it.
That groundnut bag on the shelf? Yours. Forever. Rent free.
Riddle: who'll miss NEPA? Nobody. …Me. A little.
Last show soon. I'll end with a riddle. No answer.
Final project: a radio documentary. Thirty minutes of me.
'Forty-one per cent cheaper. Source: Okafor.' Who taught me that?
Riddle me this: who's still your roommate? Me. Always.
New job. They have light all day. I don't trust it.
I passed our hall. Somebody's slippers on our floor. Ours.
Riddles After Dark, still on air. Still awake. Still you?
Freshers! Riddle: who's lost? All of you. Welcome.
Don't chase the goat. Or do. It's tradition.
Exam week. I live in the library now. Bring garri.
My brain is full. New information, please hold.
Exam week on the Ring Road. Lights low, riddles easy.
You look. I'll stand behind you. Far behind.
ALLOWANCE! Riddle: what disappears by Thursday? This.
Money came. Suya tonight. Garri tomorrow. Balance.
Market day. I'm bargaining with my last fifty naira.
Strike again? Garri, bucket, torch. We know the drill.
Indefinite, part two. The sequel nobody asked for.
Strike playlist: ten songs, all about waiting.
Cup day! I'll sing. Badly. Loudly. For the team.
Jega does left boot first. I do left slipper first. Science.
Commentary by me! Jega's through on goal… he's tied his boot.
I'm not campaigning. I'm narrating democracy.
Breaking news: roommate votes. Democracy survives.
Election night special on Ring Road FM. Bring snacks.
Convocation! Somebody's mother is crying. Everybody's mother.
Live from convocation. I'm crying on air. Don't tune out.
Iftar in ten minutes. I'm guarding the dates. Respectfully.
Sahur alarm at four. I set three. I heard none.
Half the floor went home for Christmas. More rice per person.
Valentine's. I have a date. With jollof. It's serious.
Riddle: what's red and sold out? Every rose in Kwari.
Valentine's request line is open. No riddles. …One riddle.
Harmattan. My lips have cracked. So has my spirit.
Dust on everything. Even the garri. Extra crunchy.
